records.name: One Day at a Time (ODAAT)
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps people and families dealing with addiction, housing loss and money hardship. Its services include housing help, health care, job and reentry help, and youth programs.
records.what_you_do: Ask for help with recovery, housing, health, jobs or reentry. The site does not explain intake steps, so call or email first.

first_step.how: Call (215) 226-7860 or email info@odaatphilly.org. The site does not describe intake or eligibility.
first_step.basis: Services are named, but the site does not say how someone enrolls, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: UAC's fiscal sponsorship page names ODAAT as a sponsored project, but ODAAT's own site says it is a registered 501(c)(3) with the EIN shown in match. The sponsorship status is unresolved; both facts are recorded. Support-group flag is on because this is a recovery service, so it shows only on request. The site has no dated items (its testimonials are undated), so status is probably_active under the no-dates rule. Meeting schedules are not on the site and were not recorded.

records.name: Entrepreneur Works
records.summary: A nonprofit lender and business coach for small businesses in Philadelphia and Chester. It runs workshops and business-start programs that the public can sign up for through its events calendar.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a workshop, join a business-start or pitch program, or ask the office about a small business loan or grant.

schedule.text: Workshops and events are listed on an online calendar. A Business of Art session is set for November 18, 2026, 6:30 to 7:30 pm.

cost.text: Not stated on the site; check each event page

first_step.how: Pick a workshop on the events calendar and register on its page, or use the Contact Us page.
first_step.basis: Workshops and events are open to the public with registration on each event page. Loan and grant eligibility is not listed.

records.notes: A CDFI lender that also runs public workshops. Loans and grants are for businesses, so this sits near the business line; it is listed because the workshops are open to the public. The events page lists no October 2026 events at crawl time. The Delaware County office is outside the city and is not part of this record.

records.name: Consortium Dedicated to Health Equity Education (CDHE)
records.summary: A coalition of Greater Philadelphia medical schools that works to bring more people from diverse backgrounds into medicine. It runs a yearly equity summit, a pre-med pathway for college sophomores, and a mentorship network.
records.what_you_do: Register for the yearly summit, or apply to the PADMed pathway if you are a college sophomore in the region.

schedule.text: Yearly equity summit. The 2026 summit was listed for April 7, 2026, from 8 am to 4 pm, at the College of Physicians of Philadelphia.

cost.text: Summit fee not stated on the page

first_step.how: Register for the summit through the events page, or email programs@philacdhe.org about the PADMed pathway.
first_step.basis: The summit is open to anyone who registers. The PADMed pathway needs an application.

records.notes: The site lists the April 7, 2026 summit as upcoming, which may be an old listing. The April 2026 date is recorded as the newest evidence, but it is not confirmed that the summit took place. The summit venue has no street address on the site. UAC's partner page shows a different street address (map link) and was not used.

records.name: Teenshop
records.summary: A nonprofit that prepares teenage girls for leadership through college prep, mentoring, life-skills workshops and community service. The site has join and volunteer pages and an enrollment form.
records.what_you_do: Girls can apply through the enrollment form to join programs such as workshops, college tours and community service. Volunteers can use the volunteer page.

first_step.how: Fill in the enrollment application linked from the site, or use the join page.
first_step.basis: Girls join through an enrollment application. The site does not say what a first visit is like or when programs meet.

records.notes: The site works and has join, volunteer and enrollment pages, but its only dated item is a June 15, 2020 anniversary video title, so status is dormant under the dating rules. The footer year is not used as evidence. Confirm with the group before treating this as current. UAC's partner page gives a different address (1650 Arch St), which was not used. The UAC page phone is 215-851-1843, and the site lists no phone.

records.name: COLOURS Organization
records.summary: A Philadelphia organization for queer people of color that offers health care, HIV and sexual health services, case management and support groups. It also runs named social and creative activities, including Rainbow Reads and an open mic night.
records.what_you_do: Join a support group or one of the named activities, get HIV and sexual health services, or call to ask about getting involved.

first_step.how: Call 215-832-0100 or email info@coloursorganization.org. The site does not say how to join a group or when groups meet.
first_step.basis: Activities are named, but the way in is not described on the site.

records.notes: The site lists support groups and named activities but no dates, so probably_active applies. Office hours (Monday to Friday, 10 am to 7 pm) come from the UAC partner page, not the group's site. Testing hours are not listed. The lgbtq community tag is used because the site describes queer people of color; no closer tag exists in the vocabulary. Support-group flag is off because support groups are one part of a wider health and community service.

records.name: Black Writers Museum
records.summary: A museum in the Historic Vernon House in Vernon Park that shows classic and modern Black writers and their books. It holds a free family festival in Germantown and has volunteer and donation pages.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the site's volunteer page, come to the free festival, or call to arrange a visit by appointment.

schedule.text: Museum visits by appointment. A free family festival in Germantown is held by the museum; its date is not shown on the site.

cost.text: Festival is free. Visit fees are not stated.

first_step.how: Call 267-297-3078 about volunteering, or come to a public event. Visits need an appointment.
first_step.basis: The volunteer page and the free festival are open to anyone. Museum visits need an appointment.

records.notes: The museum's own site says the Urban Affairs Coalition is its fiscal sponsor. UAC's sponsorship page does not list it, so this sponsorship was found on the project's own site. UAC's partner page says the museum runs after-school youth programs, but the museum's site does not, so none are recorded. The 2026 copyright footer is not used as evidence. No email is published on the site.

records.name: ManUpPHL
records.summary: A mentoring program that works with young men in Philadelphia who are at high risk of gun violence. Mentoring is open to young men from age 13, with a stipend, and local adults can volunteer as mentors.
records.what_you_do: Young men can ask for help through the Help Now request form. Volunteer mentors can call, email or use the volunteer form.

cost.text: Free to take part. Mentees are paid a stipend, listed on the site as $15 an hour.

first_step.how: Young men: use the Help Now request form on the site. Volunteer mentors: call 267-748-7818, email info@manupphl.org, or use the volunteer form.
first_step.basis: Mentees go through a request form, and the site does not describe what a first meeting looks like. Mentors reach out by phone, email or form.

records.notes: UAC's partner page calls ManUpPHL a program of UAC, which the group's own site does not say. The address is from the group's own site; UAC's partner page gives 1650 Arch St. The stipend amount comes from a page with no dates and may change. The site also lists a job initiative for adults up to 35, not recorded separately.

records.name: Center for Hope
records.summary: A shelter and support program for adults experiencing homelessness, with case management, life-skills help and transitional housing. Anyone can volunteer through a form on its site, and the group runs public events such as Hoops4Hope games and a Hope Shop opening.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer through the Get Involved form, donate, or check the site for games and openings. Shelter stays are for single adults referred through the City, according to the UAC partner page.

schedule.text: Listed for October on the site, with no year shown: Hope Drive from October 1 to 28, Hoops4Hope games on October 6, 13, 20 and 27, and a Hope Shop grand opening on October 15.

first_step.how: Use the Get Involved form on cfhphila.org to volunteer, or use the Contact Us page.
first_step.basis: Volunteering runs through a public form and events are public. Shelter stays need a City referral.

records.notes: The October event dates on the site have no year, so none is recorded as evidence and status stays probably_active. UAC's partner page says shelter stays are for single adults 18 and older, referred through the City, while the site speaks of the men it serves. Public volunteering and events are why this is published. The UAC page lists a different address, which was not used.

records.name: Philadelphia Family Voices
records.summary: A family-led group that helps parents and caregivers of children with behavioral health or autism challenges work with schools, benefits, insurance and other child-serving systems. Services are free to Philadelphia residents and start with a referral.
records.what_you_do: Submit the online referral form for one-on-one guidance from staff who have lived experience of these systems.

first_step.how: Submit the online referral form linked from the site.
first_step.basis: Help starts with a referral form. The site does not describe group meetings or open events.

records.notes: Support-group flag is on because this serves families of children with behavioral health or autism needs, so it shows only on request. The site has an Events section with no listings. Staff contact details are not recorded. The only date on the site is the founding year, 2020, plus a 2025 footer that is not used as evidence.

records.name: Community & Economic Development (CED)
records.summary: A department of the Urban Affairs Coalition that helps lower and moderate income families with homebuying, foreclosure prevention and money skills. It offers free financial education workshops that groups can request, and a free hotline for homeowners who are behind on payments.
records.what_you_do: Request a free money workshop for your group through the site's form, call the homeowner hotline, or sign up for a homebuyer seminar through Eventbrite.

schedule.text: Workshops are booked on request. Homebuyer seminars and fairs are registered through Eventbrite.

cost.text: Financial education workshops and the hotline are free, per the site

first_step.how: Call the hotline at 215-334-4663 if you are behind on a mortgage or property tax, or request a workshop through the site's form.
first_step.basis: The hotline and free workshops are open to the public. Groups request a workshop, and no workshop dates are listed.

records.notes: A department of the Urban Affairs Coalition, not a fiscal sponsor project. Kind is program because it offers workshops and a hotline rather than membership. Newest dated item on the site is a May 8, 2026 hotline notice. Staff email addresses on the site are not recorded. The City's HomeBuyNow program is described on the site and is not recorded separately.

records.name: Summer Youth Employment Program
records.summary: A paid summer job and internship program for Philadelphia teens ages 14 to 18. Teens apply online, complete the document and clearance steps, and are placed with employers in career tracks such as finance, science and creative arts.
records.what_you_do: Apply online at workready.org, complete the qualification and clearance steps, then attend orientation before job placement. Placement is not guaranteed.

schedule.text: Summer placements. The most recent program dates on the site are from summer 2022.

cost.text: Teens are paid for summer work. No application fee is stated.

first_step.how: Apply online at workready.org. The site lists the Philadelphia Youth Network call center at 267-502-3900.
first_step.basis: Applying, document checks and clearances come before any placement, and the site says placement is not guaranteed.

records.notes: The site shows only the summer 2022 cycle, so status is dormant under the dating rules. The program may run every year, so the current application should be checked before this is shown as active. The pay rate, dates and eligibility details come from the 2022 pages. The site's email is obscured and is not recorded.

records.name: Youth Outreach Adolescent Community Awareness Program (YO-ACAP)
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that has worked with youth and young adults for over 35 years. It runs school-based after-school clubs, paid career and construction programs, a violence intervention program, and civic programs.
records.what_you_do: Students and young adults can ask about the after-school, career and civic programs. The site does not describe the application steps, so call the office first.

cost.text: Some programs pay stipends. Fees are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Call 215-297-6206 or go to the office at 1211 Chestnut Street. The site does not describe enrollment.
first_step.basis: Program names and age ranges are listed, but enrollment steps, volunteering and open events are not described.

records.notes: Program list and age ranges come from the site. Several programs are school-based, so the audience is set to students. Entry rules for the justice-impacted young men's program and the pre-apprenticeship program are not on the site. Staff email addresses are on the site and are not recorded. The site has no dated items.

records.name: Philadelphia Anti-Drug/Anti-Violence Network (PAAN)
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works to reduce drug use and violence among young people and their families through prevention services, crisis intervention, counseling and job readiness. It holds open events such as a men's breakfast and takes sign-ups for its mailing list.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list, come to an open event such as the men's breakfast, or send a question through the site's contact form.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list, or call 215-940-0550 or use the site's contact form.
first_step.basis: Open events and a mailing list are public. Program intake steps are not described.

records.notes: The site has no event dates. Its footer shows 2019, which is not used as evidence. The address comes from UAC's partner page because the group's site does not show one. The site lists a stipend program run with a partner. The support-group flag is off because these are prevention, crisis and job readiness services, not a support group.

records.name: Everybody Builds
records.summary: A construction-industry diversity nonprofit that helps diverse contractors and workers grow, working with contractors, developers and unions.
records.notes: Business development for diverse contractors and an apprenticeship link for workers. Read as a business program rather than a community group a neighbor joins. Newest dated items are March 2024, so dormant under the dating rules. The site's Workforce Programs and Careers pages were not opened. Revisit if workforce organizations are in scope.

records.name: Achieving Reunification Center (ARC)
records.summary: A center that helps parents whose children are in foster, kinship or congregate care work toward reunification and self-sufficiency.
records.notes: Services are for parents whose children are in out-of-home placement, enrolled through a sign-up form or by child welfare staff. The site lists no public groups, classes, volunteering or open events, so there is no open public way in. Its only dated item is a 2026 footer, which is not used as evidence.

records.name: Institute for Southeast Asian Archaeology (ISEAA)
records.summary: A research institute that studies the prehistory of Southeast Asia and shares its findings with scholars and the public.
records.notes: The website on UAC's partner page (seaarchaeology.org) did not resolve when checked. The UAC page lists no programs, volunteer roles, membership or open events, and gives only an academic email and a phone number. No public way in is shown, so it is hidden.

records.name: Ready, Willing & Able Philadelphia
records.summary: A licensed residential recovery house for men with substance use disorder, where residents are placed in paid work.
records.notes: A residence rather than a group people join. The site names no application or referral route and no volunteer or open-event route. The 2024 footer and the 2019 and 2022 statistics on the site are not used as evidence of this group's activity.

records.name: Economic Development Projects (EDP)
records.summary: A consulting business that helps construction and development clients hire diverse-owned firms and local workers.
records.notes: A consulting business serving developers, not a community group. It lists no public programs, volunteering, membership or events. Only the copyright year 2026 is dated, and that is not evidence.

records.name: Haitian Relief Fund
records.summary: A group that works on rebuilding communities in Haiti through advocacy and business development.
records.notes: Its work is in Haiti, and no Philadelphia program or public way in is listed. The UAC partner page gives the same website and email as Haitian Professionals of Philadelphia, which did not resolve, so no website is recorded for this group.

notes: Scope and method: UAC's fiscal sponsorship page names two sponsored projects (One Day at a Time and Entrepreneur Works). UAC's partner directory lists 42 entries but does not say which are sponsored, so those partners were read as a partner list. The Black Writers Museum's own site says UAC is its fiscal sponsor, a link UAC's sponsorship page does not show, so UAC's sponsored list is probably longer than its page. Searches: the Allegheny West Foundation, the Philadelphia Foundation and PHMC searches found no public list of sponsored projects, so those sponsors are not covered. The City's 2026 community resilience grants page named two sponsored projects (Fernhill Food Forest under Friends of Fernhill Park; KCAP under Movement Alliance Project); both are in leads_only. The other nine City grant recipients are funded grantees, not sponsored projects, and belong to lane D. CultureWorks projects were skipped per the brief. Not checked: Entrepreneur Works Delaware County (outside the city), Center City Business Association (business association), Global Citizen (not local), PHLanthropy Week and the Thanksgiving Basket Program (annual events), City Contact Tracing and the TCIG grant program (city government), and Philadelphia City Fund (municipal sponsor only). Rate limiting: no general refusals. Only the neighborhoodsunited.net domain refused every connection, and hpphilly.org and seaarchaeology.org did not resolve. Budget: 3 of 3 searches and 58 of 60 fetches. Warning for the owner: the website printed on UAC's Healthy Town page now points to an unrelated online casino, so no record was made from that site.
